Characters in The Great Gatsby.Atticus Finch: The principled lawyer is from To Kill a Mockingbird, set in 1930s Alabama, not 1920s Long Island.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Scout Finch: The young narrator of To Kill a Mockingbird lives far from Gatsby's East Egg.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Boo Radley: The reclusive neighbour is another Harper Lee character from To Kill a Mockingbird.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Lennie Small: The gentle giant of Of Mice and Men is Steinbeck's, from a Depression-era ranch.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.George Milton: Lennie's protective friend in Of Mice and Men comes from Steinbeck, not Fitzgerald, despite a common first name with George Wilson.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Huck Finn: Twain's river-raft hero is from the 1880s and nowhere near Gatsby's West Egg.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Tom Sawyer: Twain's mischievous boy shares a first name with Tom Buchanan but not a book.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Captain Ahab: The monomaniac whale-hunter of Moby-Dick would find little to hunt on Long Island Sound.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Ishmael: The narrator of Moby-Dick opens with "Call me Ishmael", a different narrator from Nick Carraway.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Hester Prynne: Hawthorne's scarlet-letter heroine lives in 17th-century Boston, far from the Jazz Age.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Dean Moriarty: Kerouac's wild driver in On the Road is based on Neal Cassady and belongs to the Beat generation, not the Jazz Age.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Jo March: Little Women's writer heroine lives in 1860s New England, not on Long Island.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Scarlett O'Hara: The Southern belle of Gone with the Wind is set in the Civil War era, not the Roaring Twenties.
Characters in The Great Gatsby.Rhett Butler: The blockade-runner who tells Scarlett "frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn" belongs to Gone with the Wind.

Characters in Treasure Island.Jim Hawkins: The young inn-keeper's son who narrates the story finds Billy Bones's treasure map and sails to adventure.
Characters in Treasure Island.Long John Silver: The charming one-legged cook, with a parrot on his shoulder, helped create the whole image of pirates, even though Stevenson invented most of it.
Characters in Treasure Island.Captain Flint: The pirate who buried the treasure is already dead before the story begins; Silver's noisy parrot is named after him.
Characters in Treasure Island.Billy Bones: The drunken old sea dog who arrives at the Admiral Benbow inn sets the plot off by dying and leaving the map.
Characters in Treasure Island.Ben Gunn: Marooned for three years, he dreams of cheese and was once a pirate himself; he moves the treasure before the others arrive.
Characters in Treasure Island.Blind Pew: The blind beggar delivers the "black spot", the pirates' death summons, to Billy Bones.
Characters in Treasure Island.Squire Trelawney: The talkative landowner finances the expedition but boasts so loudly about it that he gives the secret away.
Characters in Treasure Island.Dr. Livesey: The sensible doctor and magistrate is a steady voice of reason, unflappable even when facing pirates.
Characters in Treasure Island.Captain Smollett: The ship's no-nonsense captain distrusts the crew from the start, and he is right.
Characters in Treasure Island.Israel Hands: Flint's former gunner, now Silver's man, tries to kill Jim aboard the Hispaniola, but Jim shoots him.
Characters in Treasure Island.Black Dog: The pirate who finds Billy Bones at the inn, wounded in a fight, is the first sign of the danger to come.
Characters in Treasure Island.Captain Hook: Barrie's hook-handed villain in Peter Pan is another famous fictional pirate, though not from Stevenson's book.
Characters in Treasure Island.Smee: Hook's bumbling boatswain in Peter Pan is a different story's pirate.
Characters in Treasure Island.Captain Ahab: Melville's whale-obsessed captain sails in Moby-Dick, not in search of treasure.
Characters in Treasure Island.Queequeg: The tattooed harpooner is Melville's, from a whaling ship, not a pirate ship.
Characters in Treasure Island.Robinson Crusoe: Defoe's castaway is stranded on an island, but there are no pirates or treasure map in his story.
Characters in Treasure Island.Captain Nemo: Verne's submarine captain has a ship of his own, the Nautilus, and lives under the sea.
Characters in Treasure Island.Gulliver: Swift's traveller has no treasure hunt in his travels.
Characters in Treasure Island.Jack Sparrow: Disney's swaggering pirate was created for 2003 and is not from a classic novel.
Characters in Treasure Island.Davy Jones: The legendary sailors' devil of the deep also appears in Pirates of the Caribbean, not Stevenson's novel.
Characters in Treasure Island.Dread Pirate Roberts: The masked pirate identity passed from man to man is from The Princess Bride, not Treasure Island.
Characters in Treasure Island.Captain Haddock: Tintin's bearded, whisky-loving, curse-prone sailor belongs to Hergé's comics.
Characters in Treasure Island.Barbossa: Sparrow's undead rival is from Disney's Pirates films, not Stevenson.
Characters in Treasure Island.Starbuck: Melville's thoughtful first mate belongs to Moby-Dick, not Treasure Island.

Things with a hole in the middle.Donut: The hole is said to have come from a ship captain named Hanson Gregory in the 1840s, so the dough cooks evenly.
Things with a hole in the middle.Bagel: Bagels are boiled briefly before baking, which gives them their shiny chewy crust, and the hole helps them cook evenly.
Things with a hole in the middle.CD: A CD's hole is 15 mm wide, and legend says the size was chosen to match a Dutch coin, which was a small one.
Things with a hole in the middle.Wedding ring: The circle of the ring has no end, which is why it has long symbolised eternity.
Things with a hole in the middle.Life Savers: The candy was designed to look like a ship's life preserver, and it was first sold in 1912.
Things with a hole in the middle.Car tire: A tire's hole is the rim opening, which is sealed airtight against the wheel, and radial tires were patented in 1946 by Michelin.
Things with a hole in the middle.Cheerio: Cheerios are a ring-shaped oat cereal first sold in 1941 as "Cheeri Oats".
Things with a hole in the middle.Metal washer: A washer spreads a bolt's load over a larger area, and the hole is what lets it slip on to the bolt.
Things with a hole in the middle.Hula hoop: The modern plastic hula hoop was a craze of 1958, and Wham-O sold millions within months.
Things with a hole in the middle.Life ring: The hole lets a person in the water slip an arm through and hold on, and it is usually bright orange or red for visibility.
Things with a hole in the middle.Pineapple ring: Ring slices are cut after the core is removed, and the core is tough and fibrous, so the hole is useful.
Things with a hole in the middle.Onion ring: Onion rings are slices of onion, and the hole is simply where the layers' centre is left empty.
Things with a hole in the middle.Vinyl record: The spindle hole in a 12-inch record is about 7 mm, and records spin at 33 and a third rpm.
Things with a hole in the middle.Pancake: Pancakes are solid discs, and the batter spreads flat on the griddle.
Things with a hole in the middle.Cookie: A classic cookie has no hole, unless it's a ring-shaped biscuit, so it is the solid sort.
Things with a hole in the middle.Quarter: A US quarter has no hole, though many coins around the world do, such as the Chinese cash coins.
Things with a hole in the middle.Pizza: Pizza is a solid disc, and a hole would just be a pizza with a hole.
Things with a hole in the middle.Frisbee: It looks like a ring but the middle is solid plastic, which is what lets it glide on air.
Things with a hole in the middle.Dinner plate: Plates are solid in the middle, and that flat centre is where the food sits.
Things with a hole in the middle.Tortilla: Tortillas are thin flat discs of corn or wheat dough, with nothing cut out.
Things with a hole in the middle.Hockey puck: A puck is a solid slab of vulcanised rubber, about 3 inches wide and weighing around 170 grams.
Things with a hole in the middle.Muffin: A muffin is a solid cake that rises in a cup, so it is a dome, not a ring.
Things with a hole in the middle.Burger bun: A bun has no hole, although the sesame seeds on it are a loose ring on top.
Things with a hole in the middle.Dartboard: A dartboard is a solid disc, and the bullseye in the middle is a target, not a hole.

Fruits with a single pit or stone.Peach: Peaches belong to the rose family and came from China; their hard pit holds a seed related to almonds.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Cherry: Cherry pits contain amygdalin, which can release cyanide if crushed and chewed, though swallowing one whole is harmless.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Plum: Plums were domesticated thousands of years ago, and a dried one is a prune; each fruit has a single hard stone.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Apricot: The kernel inside an apricot pit tastes like almond, and amaretto-style liqueurs are often flavored with it.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Mango: A mango's big flat stone is hard to cut around; the tree comes from South Asia and the fruit is India's national fruit.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Olive: Olives are stone fruits too bitter to eat raw, and some olive trees are said to live for over a thousand years.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Avocado: An avocado is botanically a single-seeded berry, and it only ripens after it has been picked.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Nectarine: A nectarine is just a peach with smooth skin, caused by a single gene variation, not a cross with a plum.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Date: Dates have one long, narrow seed, and date palms have been cultivated in the Middle East for thousands of years.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Lychee: Lychee hides a glossy brown seed under translucent white flesh, and the fruit has been grown in southern China for ages.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Apple: Apples have a core with several small seeds, not one stone, and those seeds contain a little amygdalin too.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Banana: Cultivated bananas are seedless; the tiny black specks in the middle are remnants of ovules that never matured.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Strawberry: The 'seeds' on a strawberry's skin are actually separate tiny fruits, each holding one seed, so it fits no pit rule.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Watermelon: Watermelons are packed with seeds, and seedless varieties come from sterile plants with three sets of chromosomes.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Kiwi fruit: Kiwi fruit holds dozens of tiny black seeds; it comes from China and was renamed after New Zealand's bird.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Orange: Oranges carry several seeds per fruit, except navel oranges, which are seedless and propagated by grafting.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Grape: Each grape holds a few small seeds, and most table grapes sold today are bred to have none.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Pineapple: A pineapple is really many small fruits fused together, and commercial ones are bred to have almost no seeds.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Pear: A pear's core holds small seeds, not a single stone, and like apples it belongs to the rose family.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Blueberry: Blueberries contain many tiny soft seeds, and their dusty bloom is a natural wax coating.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Pomegranate: A pomegranate holds hundreds of seeds, each wrapped in a juicy aril, the opposite of a single stone.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Fig: A fig is actually an inverted flower cluster full of tiny crunchy seeds, and many species rely on specific wasps to pollinate.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Papaya: Papaya has a central cavity of many black seeds that taste peppery and are edible.
Fruits with a single pit or stone.Tomato: Botanically a berry, a tomato holds many seeds in jelly, so it has no single stone.

Things with exactly two wheels.Bicycle: The 1817 draisine, a pedal-less ancestor of the bicycle, was pushed along with the rider's feet.
Things with exactly two wheels.Motorcycle: The first motorcycle, Daimler's 1885 Reitwagen, had a wooden frame and two main wheels plus small stabilizers.
Things with exactly two wheels.Segway: A Segway balances itself using gyroscopes and tilt sensors, and its original personal transporter ended production in 2020.
Things with exactly two wheels.Hand truck: A hand truck works like a lever; tilt it back and the load's weight rides on the axle, so you carry almost none.
Things with exactly two wheels.Chariot: Spoke-wheeled chariots appeared around 2000 BCE and changed ancient warfare.
Things with exactly two wheels.Moped: The word moped blends 'motor' and 'pedal', from the early models that could be pedaled when the engine failed.
Things with exactly two wheels.Hoverboard: Despite the name, hoverboards don't hover, and many were banned from airlines after battery fires.
Things with exactly two wheels.Dirt bike: Motocross, the racing sport for dirt bikes, began in Britain in the 1920s as 'scrambles'.
Things with exactly two wheels.Vespa: Vespa means 'wasp' in Italian, named for its buzzing engine and narrow waist; Piaggio launched it in 1946.
Things with exactly two wheels.Penny-farthing: The penny-farthing's huge front wheel covered more ground per pedal turn, and the name comes from two British coins.
Things with exactly two wheels.BMX bike: BMX stands for bicycle motocross, and it became an Olympic sport at the 2008 Beijing Games.
Things with exactly two wheels.Wheelchair: Standard wheelchairs have four wheels, two large and two small casters, while racing chairs have three.
Things with exactly two wheels.Skateboard: The first skateboards in the 1950s were roller-skate wheels nailed to planks, and all modern ones have four wheels.
Things with exactly two wheels.Tricycle: Tricycles have three wheels, which is why toddlers can ride one without learning to balance.
Things with exactly two wheels.Car: A car has four wheels, and three-wheelers like the Reliant Robin became famous for tipping over.
Things with exactly two wheels.Wagon: A wagon has four wheels, and its front axle pivots to steer.
Things with exactly two wheels.Shopping cart: The shopping cart was invented in 1937 in Oklahoma City by Sylvan Goldman and has four wheels.
Things with exactly two wheels.Unicycle: A unicycle has just one wheel, with the pedals attached directly to it.
Things with exactly two wheels.Wheelbarrow: A wheelbarrow has one wheel, and it acts as a lever; versions were used in ancient China and Greece.
Things with exactly two wheels.Roller skate: A pair of roller skates has at least four wheels, and quad skates were invented in the 1860s.
Things with exactly two wheels.Golf cart: Golf carts have four wheels and are now used on campuses, resorts and farms far from any golf course.
Things with exactly two wheels.Go-kart: Go-karts have four wheels, and the first were built by Art Ingels in California in the 1950s.
Things with exactly two wheels.Tuk-tuk: Tuk-tuks, the auto rickshaws of Asia, have three wheels and are named for the sound of their engines.
Things with exactly two wheels.Quad bike: Quad bikes are named for their four wheels, and their wide low-pressure tires are meant for rough terrain.

Things over a thousand years old.Stonehenge: Stonehenge's main stones were raised around 2500 BCE, so they are over 4,500 years old.
Things over a thousand years old.Great Pyramid: Built around 2560 BCE, the Great Pyramid is about 4,500 years old and the only ancient wonder still standing.
Things over a thousand years old.Colosseum: The Colosseum opened in 80 CE, so it has stood for nearly 2,000 years.
Things over a thousand years old.Parthenon: The Parthenon was completed in 432 BCE and was heavily damaged in 1687 when a Venetian shell hit stored gunpowder.

Things over a thousand years old.Tutankhamun's mask: Tutankhamun's gold mask is over 3,300 years old and weighs more than 10 kilograms.

Things over a thousand years old.Hagia Sophia: Hagia Sophia was completed in 537 CE, and for nearly a thousand years its dome was the largest in the world.
Things over a thousand years old.Pompeii ruins: Pompeii was buried by Vesuvius in 79 CE, preserving everyday life for nearly 2,000 years.
Things over a thousand years old.Mona Lisa: The Mona Lisa dates from the early 1500s, only about 500 years old.

Things over a thousand years old.Tower of London: The Tower of London was begun around 1078 under William the Conqueror, making it just under 950 years old.

Traditional wedding anniversary themes.Paper: The first anniversary gift is paper, and it recalls a clean page at the start of a marriage, while the 25th is silver.

Traditional wedding anniversary themes.Wood: Wood for year five stands for a marriage rooted and growing, the sturdy start of a family tree.

Traditional wedding anniversary themes.China: China marks year twenty, and its fragility and beauty were meant to stand for a union that is both precious and breakable.
Traditional wedding anniversary themes.Silver: Silver marks 25 years, and a silver wedding is still celebrated widely in Europe and beyond.
Traditional wedding anniversary themes.Pearl: Pearl marks year thirty, and it is one of the few gems made by a living creature, an oyster coating an irritant.
Traditional wedding anniversary themes.Ruby: Ruby marks forty years, and the deep-red stone has long symbolised passion that endures.
